title: Impact of Major Product Recall on Stock Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Event Study using the market model. Compute abnormal returns (AR) as realized stock returns minus expected returns given market movements. For the focal firm (the recall announcer), cumulate AR over short windows around the announcement to obtain CAR and test significance.
- Why: A recall announcement is a sharp, well-timed information shock. Event studies isolate its impact on equity value over very short windows when other confounders are minimal and markets are efficient.
- Key assumptions:
  - Market efficiency over short windows: prices incorporate news quickly, so AR reflect the recall’s impact.
  - Correct expected return model over the short horizon: beta is stable and the market model is well-specified; we also absorb any intercept (alpha) using the pre-event window.
  - No other firm-specific confounding news for the treated firm during the event window.
  - For robustness, a DiD on AR with firm and event-day fixed effects nets out any common shocks that remain after market-model adjustment.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s62_data.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Basic checks
stopifnot(all(c("stock_id","event_day","ret","mkt_ret","beta") %in% names(df)))

# Assumption: the first stock_id in the file is the recall firm (adjust if known)
treated_id <- sort(unique(df$stock_id))[1]

# Estimate per-stock alpha from pre-event days using provided beta
pre <- subset(df, event_day < 0)
pre$excess <- pre$ret - pre$beta * pre$mkt_ret
alpha_by <- aggregate(excess ~ stock_id, data = pre, FUN = function(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))
names(alpha_by)[2] <- "alpha_hat"
df <- merge(df, alpha_by, by = "stock_id", all.x = TRUE)
# If a stock has no pre-event data (unlikely), set alpha_hat to 0
df$alpha_hat[is.na(df$alpha_hat)] <- 0

# Abnormal returns (market model with alpha)
df$AR <- df$ret - df$alpha_hat - df$beta * df$mkt_ret

# Treated firm series
tr <- subset(df, stock_id == treated_id)
n_pre <- sum(tr$event_day < 0 & !is.na(tr$AR))
s_pre <- sd(tr$AR[tr$event_day < 0], na.rm = TRUE)

# Helper to compute CAR, t, p
car_test <- function(ev_days, ar_vec, day_vec, s_pre, df_t) {
  idx <- which(day_vec %in% ev_days & !is.na(ar_vec))
  L <- length(idx)
  if (L == 0 || is.na(s_pre) || s_pre == 0) return(list(CAR=NA, t=NA, p=NA, L=L))
  CAR <- sum(ar_vec[idx])
  tstat <- CAR / (s_pre * sqrt(L))
  pval <- 2 * (1 - pt(abs(tstat), df = max(df_t - 1, 1)))
  list(CAR=CAR, t=tstat, p=pval, L=L)
}

# Main event windows
w_same_day <- 0:0
w_m1_p1 <- -1:1
w_0_p2 <- 0:2

# Compute AR-based metrics for treated firm
ar0 <- tr$AR[tr$event_day == 0]
ar0 <- ifelse(length(ar0) > 0, ar0[1], NA_real_)
t_ar0 <- ifelse(!is.na(s_pre) && s_pre > 0, ar0 / s_pre, NA_real_)
p_ar0 <- ifelse(!is.na(t_ar0), 2 * (1 - pt(abs(t_ar0), df = max(n_pre - 1, 1))), NA_real_)

res_m1_p1 <- car_test(w_m1_p1, tr$AR, tr$event_day, s_pre, n_pre)
res_0_p2  <- car_test(w_0_p2,  tr$AR, tr$event_day, s_pre, n_pre)

# Placebo check: average AR of controls at day 0
controls <- subset(df, stock_id != treated_id)
aar0_controls <- mean(controls$AR[controls$event_day == 0], na.rm = TRUE)

# Robustness 1: Market-adjusted returns (without beta/alpha)
df$MAR <- df$ret - df$mkt_ret
tr_mar <- subset(df, stock_id == treated_id)
s_pre_mar <- sd(tr_mar$MAR[tr_mar$event_day < 0], na.rm = TRUE)
idx_w <- which(tr_mar$event_day %in% w_m1_p1 & !is.na(tr_mar$MAR))
L_mar <- length(idx_w)
car_mar <- ifelse(L_mar > 0, sum(tr_mar$MAR[idx_w]), NA_real_)
t_car_mar <- ifelse(!is.na(s_pre_mar) && s_pre_mar > 0 && L_mar > 0, car_mar / (s_pre_mar * sqrt(L_mar)), NA_real_)
p_car_mar <- ifelse(!is.na(t_car_mar), 2 * (1 - pt(abs(t_car_mar), df = sum(tr_mar$event_day < 0 & !is.na(tr_mar$MAR)) - 1)), NA_real_)

# Robustness 2: DiD on AR with firm and day fixed effects
df$Treat <- as.integer(df$stock_id == treated_id)
df$D0 <- as.integer(df$event_day == 0) * df$Treat
df$D_m1p1 <- as.integer(df$event_day %in% w_m1_p1) * df$Treat

did_mod_D0 <- lm(AR ~ D0 + factor(stock_id) + factor(event_day), data = df)
did_mod_Dw <- lm(AR ~ D_m1p1 + factor(stock_id) + factor(event_day), data = df)

get_coefs <- function(mod, nm) {
  s <- summary(mod)$coefficients
  if (!(nm %in% rownames(s))) return(c(Estimate=NA, SE=NA, p=NA))
  c(Estimate = s[nm, "Estimate"],
    SE       = s[nm, "Std. Error"],
    p        = s[nm, "Pr(>|t|)"])
}

did0 <- get_coefs(did_mod_D0, "D0")
didw <- get_coefs(did_mod_Dw, "D_m1p1")
# Convert average daily DiD effect over -1:+1 to CAR by multiplying by L
L_w <- length(w_m1_p1)
didw_CAR <- c(CAR_Est = didw["Estimate"] * L_w,
              CAR_SE  = didw["SE"] * L_w,
              CAR_p   = didw["p"])

# Print results
cat(sprintf("Treated firm (stock_id = %s)\n", treated_id))
cat("Market-model abnormal returns (AR) using pre-event alpha and provided beta:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Day 0 AR: %.4f  (t = %.2f, p = %.4f)\n", ar0, t_ar0, p_ar0))
cat(sprintf("  CAR[-1,+1]: %.4f  (t = %.2f, p = %.4f; L = %d)\n",
            res_m1_p1$CAR, res_m1_p1$t, res_m1_p1$p, res_m1_p1$L))
cat(sprintf("  CAR[0,+2]:  %.4f  (t = %.2f, p = %.4f; L = %d)\n",
            res_0_p2$CAR,  res_0_p2$t,  res_0_p2$p,  res_0_p2$L))

cat("\nPlacebo check (controls' average AR at day 0):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Controls' AAR at day 0: %.4f\n", aar0_controls))

cat("\nRobustness 1: Market-adjusted returns (ret - mkt_ret):\n")
cat(sprintf("  CAR[-1,+1]: %.4f  (t = %.2f, p = %.4f; L = %d)\n",
            car_mar, t_car_mar, p_car_mar, L_mar))

cat("\nRobustness 2: DiD on AR with firm and day fixed effects:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Incremental AR on day 0 (DiD): %.4f  (SE = %.4f, p = %.4f)\n",
            did0["Estimate"], did0["SE"], did0["p"]))
cat(sprintf("  Avg daily effect over [-1,+1] (DiD): %.4f  (SE = %.4f, p = %.4f)\n",
            didw["Estimate"], didw["SE"], didw["p"]))
cat(sprintf("  Implied CAR[-1,+1] (DiD): %.4f  (SE = %.4f, p = %.4f)\n",
            didw_CAR["CAR_Est"], didw_CAR["CAR_SE"], didw_CAR["CAR_p"]))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative abnormal returns for the recall firm at and immediately after the announcement.
- Magnitude: Day 0 AR around -1% to -2%; CAR over [-1,+1] around -1.5% to -3.5%, depending on severity and visibility of the recall. Controls’ AAR at day 0 should be near zero. Robustness via market-adjusted returns and DiD on AR should confirm a materially negative, statistically significant effect.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: We analyze the change in cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) around the recall announcement event.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The product recall announcement leads to a significant negative impact on the company's stock returns.
